title: Wall Street Analysts See a 25.64% Upside in Snowflake (SNOW): Can the Stock Really Move This High?
author: Zacks.Com
description: Snowflake (SNOW) has gained 0.5% over the past four weeks and currently trades at $338.99. Wall Street analysts have set a mean price target of $425.91, suggesting a potential 25.6% upside. The stock holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating, supported by positive earnings estimate revisions, though the article cautions that price targets alone should not be the sole basis for investment decisions.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate increased 2.5%, suggesting analyst optimism about the company's earnings prospects.

title: Why Is Snowflake (SNOW) Down 4.1% Since Last Earnings Report?
author: Na
description: Snowflake reported Q2 fiscal 2027 earnings of $0.62 per share, beating estimates by 37.78%, with revenues of $1.55 billion up 35.1% year-over-year. AI products contributed roughly half of growth acceleration, with CoCo accounts surpassing 9,100. The company raised full-year product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion (36% growth) and operating margin outlook to 14.5%. Despite a 4.1% share decline over the past month, analyst estimates have trended upward, earning the stock a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

title: Can Oracle's Database Business Sustain Margins over the Long Term?
author: Na
description: Oracle's multicloud database revenues surged 353% year-over-year as it shifts from traditional licenses to pay-per-use cloud pricing. However, the transition pressures margins through declining legacy software revenues and capital-intensive infrastructure buildout, resulting in negative free cash flow of $5 billion. MongoDB and Snowflake demonstrate stronger margin expansion in consumption-based models without similar infrastructure costs.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong revenue growth (30%) and multicloud database expansion (353%) are offset by declining legacy software revenues (-3%), negative free cash flow (-$5B), and margin sustainability concerns. Stock down 29.2% YTD with Hold rating reflects mixed outlook on whether consumption-based growth can offset infrastructure costs.
